evals.prompt: Design a PostgreSQL table for meeting-room reservations. Each reservation has a room, a start time, and an end time. The database itself must guarantee that two reservations for the same room can never overlap in time. Write the CREATE TABLE statement.
assertions: Uses an EXCLUDE USING GIST exclusion constraint to prevent overlaps (not a trigger, application check, or plain UNIQUE constraint)
The exclusion constraint compares the room identifier WITH = and a range type (e.g. tstzrange over start/end) WITH the && overlap operator

evals.prompt: We have a products table with tens of millions of rows and an API endpoint that lets users page through them ordered by created_at descending. The current implementation uses LIMIT with a page offset and gets slower on deeper pages. Rewrite the pagination query so it stays fast on any page.
assertions: Uses keyset/cursor pagination with a WHERE clause comparing the ordering column to the last-seen value (e.g. WHERE created_at < $last_seen) plus ORDER BY and LIMIT
Does not rely on OFFSET for skipping rows

evals.prompt: This query is doing a sequential scan and is slow on a large users table: SELECT * FROM users WHERE lower(email) = 'user@example.com'. There is already a B-tree index on the email column but the planner ignores it. Add an index that makes this query use an index scan.
assertions: Creates an expression/functional index on LOWER(email) (e.g. CREATE INDEX ... ON users (LOWER(email)))
Explains or implies that the existing plain index on email is unusable because the predicate wraps the column in lower()

evals.prompt: Set up a PostgreSQL readwrite role for an application in the public schema. The application user must be able to SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all existing tables, on any tables created later without re-granting, and it must be able to insert into tables that use identity/serial columns. Provide the SQL.
assertions: Uses ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public so future tables inherit the grants automatically
Grants USAGE (or ALL) on sequences to the role so nextval works for identity/serial columns
Grants privileges to a role and then assigns that role to the user rather than granting directly to the user
